status: Reviewed source-fit authoring tasks for B1.1/B1.2/B3.4; three scoped associations using two shared claims. This does not certify learner attainment or all Grade3 coverage.
scope: Ontario Grade 3, ages8–9. Two contemporary Ontario regional cases including a First Nation; no assumption of a single occupation, culture or land-use pattern for everyone.

checkedFacts: The Nation describes fish assessment, marine/land monitoring and fisheries management work associated with Lake Nipissing, as well as forestry responsibilities.
Its own dated MOU account describes collaboration with Ontario, resource monitoring and a walleye population still requiring recovery.
limits: The MOU narrative refers to March2022; early recovery signs are not proof of a later completed recovery.
Neither resource availability nor department existence establishes the occupation of every resident, all employment shares, or a legal entitlement for the reader.
Do not describe the First Nation as a municipality subordinate to a neighbouring town.

checkedFacts: The Nation describes a local economy with member-owned enterprises, business support and infrastructure work.
Its account names sustainable forestry/natural resources and a commercial/light-industrial business park among its projects.
limits: This is the Nation’s account, not an independently estimated employment census.
Use the described types of work; do not invent percentages, rank every sector, or assume every announced project has reached a later outcome.

checkedFacts: The agency’s October2026 account documents tourism/visitor services work around Niagara attractions, alongside maintenance and year-round versus seasonal employment.
The account links visitor revenue to operating and attraction investment.
limits: This is one regional employer, not the whole Niagara labour market.
Niagara Falls and its river setting help explain the tourism case, but the source does not show that physical geography determines every job or that all residents work in tourism.
Do not turn the account into a requirement to travel, buy tickets or forecast next year’s employment.

resources.publisher: Nipissing First Nation and Niagara Parks
checkedFacts: Nipissing First Nation identifies its location on Lake Nipissing’s north shore between North Bay and West Nipissing, with multiple communities across its land base.
Niagara Parks identifies its attractions and parkland along the Niagara River between Fort Erie and Niagara-on-the-Lake, including the Horseshoe Falls setting.
limits: A community/provider account establishes the selected location and activities, not a complete municipal, legal or traditional-territory boundary.
Niagara Parks’ analogy to a city within a city does not turn it into a municipal government.
Use the dated October2026 employment account for that year; do not combine older undated staffing figures into an invented current total.

adultPreparation: Supply an accurately attributed regional reference map and concise dated accounts for Nipissing First Nation/Lake Nipissing and Niagara Falls/Niagara Parks. Verify the selected locations and distinguish community, municipality, lake and provider service area.

Prepare job/activity cards drawn from the actual accounts, including fisheries assessment/monitoring, forestry, small-business support and tourism/visitor services/maintenance. State what each worker does; avoid unsourced precise pay or resident data.

Include a second same-region type of work not reducible to the headline natural feature, so the task does not imply environmental determinism. Use the Nation’s own business/infrastructure account for that contrast.
learnerTask: Identify and describe several documented types of work in each selected region and explain how the work serves people. Keep paid work and voluntary participation distinct where the supplied account does.

For each region, explain a supported connection from a physical feature to an activity and work opportunity: lake/fishery to monitoring/fisheries work, and falls/river visitor destination to tourism/services. Point to the supplied evidence for the link.
Contrast a supplied business/infrastructure role with the headline natural-resource or tourism role. Explain that the natural environment provides opportunities but is not the only influence on work.

Use a simple comparison table linking actual region, feature, activity/work and supporting source. Present a supported conclusion and one reasonable evidence-based prediction, plus what extra source would improve confidence.
taskProtocol.positive: Describes documented work in both regions, including the First Nation, and explains supported feature→activity/work connections without turning them into universal claims.
nearMiss: Lists jobs without connecting them to the supplied region or feature.
Assumes every First Nation resident fishes or every Niagara resident works in tourism.
Treats a hoped-for recovery, a provider’s seasonal workforce or a project announcement as a universal current outcome.
taskProtocol.transfer: Use a fresh accurate account of another Ontario region and distinguish a supported environment/work connection from an unsupported claim about all residents. No memorized regional list alone establishes transfer.
taskProtocol.authoringEvidenceBoundary: The protocol accounts for required resource and regional performance conditions as a designed task. It neither reports a child completing it nor requires a classroom attainment study before an authoring judgment.

contributingClaims.role: Work types and what people do; existing whole claim also includes earning money and interests, which remain intact. The regional task is a contribution, not a claim that the whole topic was mastered.
Physical/managed/built feature discrimination contributes to reading the selected setting; it does not supply every land-use purpose.
Regional location and interconnection representation; keep the whole map/flow claim and legal-boundary limits intact.
Evidence-backed explanation, prediction and method/source improvement. Its general inquiry claim is not confined to the experiment used in its parent prompt.

notChanged: No existing authored claim, old context or interval, dependency, catalogue, research or learner state changed.
The shared supporting map, feature and inquiry claims remain unmodified; the regional task does not certify mastery of their full claims.
All other Grade3 historical, governance, population-pattern, print-and-digital thematic-map and inquiry conditions remain separately reviewed.

associationChanges.wholeClaimFit: Both whole claims remain unchanged; only exact-band source associations are added. The regional tasks contribute rather than certify full topic mastery.

adultPreparation: Retain actual Nation-authored LakeNipissing/NFN location, fisheries/resources and business/infrastructure accounts, and actual NiagaraParks river/falls location and tourism accounts.

Supply accurately labelled map/photos and own-word factual cards: lake/fish habitat→documented fishing/monitoring use; falls/river attraction→documented visitor/recreation/parkland use. A provider account is not the whole region or a land-ownership/legal-use map.
Include actual Nation business/infrastructure example to show not every use or decision is fixed by the headline natural feature.
learnerTask: Describe the actual physical feature in each case and the documented use of the place/water, then explain the feature→activity/use connection and need/want served.
Compare the two different connections without claiming every resident has the same occupation, all forests have one use, or natural features uniquely determine the community.
Explain what additional information would be needed to establish an ambiguous new site’s actual use; do not read purpose from colour/cover alone.
landUseRelationshipTask.positive: Explains supported lake/resource and falls/visitor-use relationships and distinct purposes; retains actual provider/regional limits.
landUseRelationshipTask.transfer: Use a new accurate Ontario place account with an explicit documented natural feature/use relationship and a second plausible but unsupported use; distinguish what evidence supports.
